# One early swing, one narrow moment, and a complete Hanshin win

On August 16, Hanshin played Hiroshima at Mazda Stadium. Hanshin won 8–1, but the game was not simply decided in one moment.

Hanshin moved first in the opening inning. Teruaki Sato hit a two-run home run to center field. Hanshin led 2–0 before the game had time to settle.

That early lead needed support. Hanshin’s starter, Ryoto Ihara, worked five innings. He allowed only two hits and one run. Hiroshima scored that run in the fifth inning.

Hanshin did not stop after the early lead. The team scored again in the seventh and eighth innings. Hiroshima had no more runs, and the gap grew wider late in the game.

So this win had two parts. Sato opened the game with power. Then Hanshin kept control until the final score was clear.

## A narrow moment in the middle

In the fifth inning, Hiroshima came within one run. Elehuris Montero hit a solo home run, making the score 2–1. At that point, Hanshin still had to protect a small lead before the later scoring created a much wider gap.

### A team effort, not one big swing

The late attack came from more than one player. Seishiro Sakamoto drove in a run in the seventh, and pinch-hitter Torai Fushimi added an RBI hit. Sakamoto then struck again with an RBI double in the eighth. The final separation was built by repeated contributions, not only by the opening home run.

## In one line…

Hanshin opened fast, held its narrow lead through the middle of the game, and finished with a team-built 8–1 victory.
